title: Euler characteristic of a nodal curve from its normalization
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $B$ be a proper reduced connected $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-weil-connected-scheme], nodal at every nonsmooth point in the sense that its completed local rings are $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $B_1,\ldots,B_v$ be its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. For each $i$, let $\widetilde B_i\to B_i$ be the normalization [def-sc-normalization], assumed smooth proper connected, and put $g_i=\dim_k H^1(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O_{\widetilde B_i})$ [def-sc-genus]. Let $e$ be the number of internal nodes of $B$, counting a self-node once. Then, for the Euler characteristic of the structure sheaf [def-pc-euler-characteristic], $$\chi(B)=v-e-\sum_{i=1}^{v}g_i.$$

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), normalization exact sequence; curves.tex Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), the completed split-node model. Its normalization quotient is k[[u]] direct-sum k[[v]] modulo the pairs with equal constant term, hence one copy of k. Summing normalized-component Euler characteristics gives the formula.

proof.text: Let $\nu:\widetilde B=\coprod_i\widetilde B_i\to B$ be the normalization map. The supporting normalization-quotient lemma [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-quotient] supplies a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_B\to\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde B}\to Q\to0$ of coherent modules and gives $\chi(B,Q)=e$.

Apply Euler additivity [lem-pc-euler-additive] to Step 1. Since a finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], the cohomology edge isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] for $\nu$ identify $H^j(B,\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde B})$ with $H^j(\widetilde B,\mathcal O_{\widetilde B})$ in every degree, linearly over $k$. Taking alternating dimensions gives $\chi(B)=\chi(\widetilde B)-e$. For the open-and-closed component inclusions $j_i:\widetilde B_i\to\widetilde B$, the structure sheaf is $\bigoplus_i j_{i,*}\mathcal O_{\widetilde B_i}$. Apply Euler additivity to its finite split direct-sum filtration and the same affine edge isomorphisms to the finite morphisms $j_i$. Thus $\chi(B)=\sum_i\chi(\widetilde B_i)-e$.

Each $\widetilde B_i$ is proper over $k$, hence of finite type, and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its dimension is one. Therefore [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^j(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O)=0$ for every $j\ge2$. For the smooth proper connected curve $\widetilde B_i$, [lem-sc-global-functions] gives $H^0(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O)=k$, and [def-sc-genus] gives $\dim_kH^1(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O)=g_i$. The Euler sum [def-pc-euler-characteristic] consequently has exactly the degree-zero and degree-one contributions: $\chi(\widetilde B_i)=1-g_i$.

proof.text: Substituting the component values into Step 2 yields $\chi(B)=\sum_i(1-g_i)-e=v-e-\sum_{i=1}^v g_i$, as claimed. The formula also counts a self-node once because the supporting quotient lemma has one local quotient copy of $k$ for each singular point.
